subject: Re: EdenHealth trial environment selection & success criteria
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@edenhealth.com>, EdenHealth IT <it@edenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdenHealth discovery — environment options, proposed eval plan (recap & next steps)

Hi Sanjay / Eden IT team — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned heading into a trial: 

Recap of environment options discussed:
- Hosted (Redwood-hosted API): fastest to start, no infra changes required from Eden. Good for rapid functional validation but not ideal if you need network isolation or strict data residency.
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity in our infra): predictable throughput with dedicated GPUs; good middle ground for performance-sensitive workloads, supports private data handling controls.
- VPC trial (customer-managed VPC / Private deployment): full network isolation, SSO/KMS integration, best for HIPAA/regulatory setups — requires some network prep (firewall rules, peering) and takes longer to spin up.

Suggested evaluation plan (4-week cadence):
1) Week 0: Kickoff & environment setup — decide between Hosted / Dedicated / VPC and exchange any compliance docs (BAA request noted).
2) Week 1: Baseline tests — sample dataset ingest, latency/throughput profiling, core prompts.
3) Week 2: Workload stress — concurrent sessions, long-context runs, KV cache behaviors.
4) Week 3: Quality & regression checks — run subset of clinical prompts, measure hallucination / factuality metrics.
5) Week 4: Final review & success gating — compare against success criteria and decide go/no-go.

Proposed success criteria (examples — please review and edit):
- Latency: median 95th-percentile < 320ms for common query profile (100 token responses) on dedicated sandbox; Hosted target < 220ms.
- Throughput: sustain 10 QPS with < 5% tail latency spikes.
- Quality: pass 90% of the curated 120 clinical prompt tests (precision / factuality baseline).
- Cost: per-request cost estimate within agreed range (Ben to provide numbers).
- Security: BAA in place (if required) and network controls validated for VPC.

Immediate asks for Eden to confirm: 
1) Which environment do you want to pursue for the 4-week trial (Hosted | Dedicated sandbox | VPC trial)?
2) If VPC, please share the network owner contact and available maintenance windows for peering/peering tests.
3) Confirmation on target dataset and whether test data will be de-identified.

Attachments: eden-trial-eval-checklist.xlsx (initial checklist), network-firewall-reqs.txt (typical ports/CIDRs we request).

Next steps I’ll take after you confirm environment:
- If Hosted/Dedicated: provision trial workspace and share credentials + sample prompts within 48 hours.
- If VPC: schedule network prep call and share a runbook for peering; estimated lead time 7–10 business days.

Thanks — looking forward to your preference.

Best,
Rishi

Thanks Rishi — good writeup and very helpful. A couple of clarifications from IT and security: 

- Our compliance team prefers a VPC-based trial given PHI risk and the requirement to sign a BAA. Is Redwood able to run a time-limited VPC sandbox under a trial contract?
- What specific lead time should we plan for our network team? You mentioned 7–10 business days — is that realistic if we push this week?
- Can you provide a high-level cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC for a 4-week pilot (ballpark)? If possible, put numbers next to the examples in your checklist (we need to budget).

Also attaching the name of our network owner: Janet Liu <janet.liu@edenhealth.com>. She’ll coordinate the firewall rules and peering with your ops contact.

Quick answers: we will use a de-identified subset for quality checks initially; later phases may require a small amount of live data under BAA.

Looking forward to the SLA and an estimated timeline.

—Sanjay
Head of Product — Clinical AI
EdenHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: EdenHealth VPC trial ops notes (owners & action items)

Looping internal owners — quick internal plan based on Sanjay’s ask for a VPC-based trial.

Operational owners (proposed):
- Network / Peering + Firewall configuration: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.ai) — coordinate with Janet Liu at Eden.
- Private deployment provisioning & infra: Marissa Cole — prepares the private control plane workspace.
- Security & compliance / BAA intake: Rishi (ownership on negotiation) and Legal (I’ll loop Legal once we have confirmation).
- Cost estimate & capacity sizing: Ben — please produce an itemized 4-week estimate (VM/GPU hours, egress, support hours).

Proposed technical checklist for the VPC trial (expand as needed):
- Exchange IP ranges and set up peering (we use: 34.201.0.0/16 as example) — see network-firewall-reqs.txt.
- SAML/SSO: Eden to provide IdP metadata for SSO (optional for pilot).
- KMS key access (if they want customer-managed keys): confirm KMS ARN and admin contact.
- Test dataset placement: agreed de-identified sample in S3 bucket owned by Eden; grant our service account read access.
- Monitoring: enable trial-level logs; Marissa to provision console access with token-level billing turned on.

Success metrics suggestions (we should align these with product metrics):
- Latency (p95), throughput (sustained QPS), model output quality (per the 120 case tests), and reliability (uptime % during trial).

Ben — can you turn around the cost sheet and a short SLA addendum we can attach to the trial order? I’ve added a note to include a limited support-response SLA (4 business-hour initial response) for the pilot.

Thanks — I’ll prepare a short kickoff agenda once we have confirmation and Janet’s availability.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
